sub_graphs.title: MODEXP Precompile: Complex Gas Calculation
sub_graphs.description: Models the EIP-2565 gas cost formula based on operand sizes and exponent bit length

nodes.label: Operands Ready for Gas Calc
nodes.description: Base, exponent, and modulus lengths are available for gas calculation

nodes.label: Compute Multiplication Complexity
nodes.description: Calculate max(base_length, mod_length) rounded to 8-byte words, squared

nodes.label: Compute Iteration Count
nodes.description: Determine iterations from exponent bit length (special handling for exp > 32 bytes)

nodes.label: Read First 32 Exponent Bytes
nodes.description: Extract up to first 32 bytes of exponent for bit length calculation

nodes.label: Compute Adjusted Iteration Count
nodes.description: Apply formula: if exp_len > 32, add 8 * (exp_len - 32) to bit length

nodes.label: Compute Final Gas Cost
nodes.description: Calculate max(200, (complexity * iterations) / 3)

ambiguities.text: The precompile address (0x05) is not explicitly stated in the module documentation
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume address 0x05 based on EIP-198 specification. Verify against precompile mapping module.

ambiguities.text: The behavior when input data is shorter than 96 bytes (insufficient for length fields) is not explicitly defined
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume zero-padding behavior applies even for the initial 96 bytes, meaning missing length fields are treated as zero.

ambiguities.text: The term 'iteration count' in gas calculation refers to bit-length-based work but exact formula details vary by EIP version
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume EIP-2565 formula is used: iteration_count = max(0, (exponent_bit_length - 1) + 8 * max(0, exp_length - 32)).

implicit_assumptions.description: Python's built-in pow(base, exp, mod) is cryptographically correct for all input sizes
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect modular exponentiation could break RSA signature verification and other cryptographic operations relying on MODEXP

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot exploit the quadratic gas formula to cause out-of-memory conditions before gas is exhausted
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Memory exhaustion attack if very large length values are provided that pass gas check but exhaust node memory

implicit_assumptions.description: The minimum gas cost of 200 prevents zero-cost abuse even for trivial inputs
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If minimum gas could be bypassed, attackers could spam MODEXP calls with trivial inputs

implicit_assumptions.description: The gas formula accurately reflects computational cost across all input size combinations
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Underpriced gas for certain input patterns could enable DoS, overpriced gas could make legitimate use uneconomical
